"I and Thou" is the centerpiece of Buber's groundbreaking philosophy. It lays out a view of the world in which human beings can enter into relationships using their innermost and whole being to form true partnerships. These deep forms of rapport contrast with those that spring from the Industrial Revolution, namely the common, but basically unethical, treatment of others as objects for our use and the incorrect view of the universe as merely the object of our senses. Buber goes on to demonstrate how these interhuman meetings are a reflection of the human meeting with God. For Buber, the essence of biblical religion consists in the fact that -- regardless of the infinite abyss between them -- a dialogue between man and God is possible.
Heavily influenced by the writings of Frederich Nietzsche, Martin Buber united the proto-Existentialists currents of modern German thought with the Judeo-Christian tradition, powerfully updating faith for modern times.

**Join us to discuss this classic book over the course of 4-weeks!**

Week 1 Sat 4/12 12:30-2:30pm \*in the Seahorse Room
Week 2 Sat 4/19 12:30-2:30pm
Week 3 Sat 4/26 12:30-2:30pm
Week 4 Sat 4/3 12:30-2:30pm

**Reading for Week 1**
Finish the rest of Part 1 Aphorisms 15-29 (roughly 18 pages)

**\*A couple notes about the reading:**

1. **Translation**
Feel free to read any translation of the book you like. I will be reading both the Walter Kaufman Translation [free pdf here ](https://theanarchistlibrary.org/library/martin-buber-i-and-thou)
and The Ronald Gregor Smith Translation [free pdf here](http://uploads.worldlibrary.net/uploads/pdf/20110831000408iandthou.pdf)
2. **Aphorisms**
The Aphorisms are not numbered. They are just given bullet points or are separated by spaces depending on the version you're reading. The first Aphorism we'll discuss this week begins...
"*In the face of Directness..." -* in the Gregor Smith Translation

3. **Supplementary Sources**
Finally, though the reading is fairly short —it is quite dense. Therefore, I will be reading a few **supplementary sources** to help me understand the text. I'll link below to the ones I'm using, but feel free to use others and to share any good sources you come across in the comments! (:

* Martin Buber's I and Thou: Practicing Living Dialogue by Kenneth Paul Kramer (book) [here](https://www.amazon.com/dp/0809141582?ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_fed_asin_title)
* I and Thou Sparknotes [here](https://www.sparknotes.com/philosophy/iandthou/themes/)
* Eric Dodson lectures (youtube) [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6MIEh6Buv_E)

We follow a mindful conversation approach, details on this along with a general FAQ on how we run the meetup can be found [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1dfefKv8HVAvyeXOvk1k8ihRqml5jnrI3mbvU-D6i0iA/edit?usp=sharing).
Reading is required to participate in the discussion, but not required to attend.

Can't wait discuss these ideas with all of you!
-Zach

Hi to all,

I've been flirting with scheduling a reading of this for a while and now, having established a decent amount of interest in this spiritual series, I figured it was time to dive into the controversial self-proclaimed *superfascista* **Julius Evola** and his esoteric far-right philosophical survival manual for modernity, *Ride the Tiger: A Survival Manual for the Aristocrats of the Soul.* How better to lose my readership than this?

Heavily inspired by the Traditionalist philosophy of **René Guénon** \- our first reading in this adventure \- and **Friedrich Nietzsche**, Evola's final text is written against the backdrop of the Second World War, the failure of Fascism, the rise of materialism, secularism, and moral decline - all of which Evola swiftly describes as an *age of dissolution.* Somewhat similar to **Simone Weil's** *self-emptying attention* recently discussed in our reading of *[On the Abolition of All Political Parties](https://www.meetup.com/reading-philosophy/events/306784085/?eventOrigin=your_events),* Evola advances in his twilight years a notion of *apoliteia*, an inner distance unassailable by society and its (as he perceives it) increasingly amoralistic and barbaric attitudes and values, a stance unaccepting of anything binding one to the present, etc. As with all of our thinkers, Evola is pursuing *transcendence*, via a defense of the world of *being* and *dignity* of those *aristocrats* who feel they belong to a different modality of humanity, wherein one might exist in full recognition of *the desert* that surrounds us, enabling us to "*ride the tiger*" so that we might supra-navigate the chaos and degeneration of the modern, technologically-saturated world that we're so unfortunate to inhabit. Or something like that, I don't know.

We will be reading through **Part 4** (*Dissolution of the Individual*) for this meet-up so **18) *The "Animal Ideal" - The Sentiment of Nature*** should be the last section read.

I will be reading Godwin and Fontana's translation published by Inner Traditions. It is available [through this guy's website who recently lost like 12% of his net-worth as a result of tariffs](https://www.amazon.com/Ride-Tiger-Survival-Manual-Aristocrats/dp/0892811250) (lol).
Also [available for free here](https://www.cakravartin.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2006/08/Julius-Evola-Ride-the-Tiger-Survival-Manual-for-the-Aristocrats-of-the-Soul.pdf) but please help Jeff get his money back up if you can.

As always, if you're unable to complete the book prior to our meeting, no worries - it's lengthy so we're just happy to have you and welcome whatever insights, critiques, questions, etc. you may have based on what you were able to read.

We will be meeting in the **Ace Hotel lobby** on W 29th. It's cozy, there are couches, there is lunch, there is wine (thank god) and there is a Stumptown Coffee in the front. It's great. Message me the day of if you can't find us. I usually sit toward the back next to the bar.

It bears repeating, this group is open to newcomers to Evola (preferred in this case), novices of philosophy, ragamuffins, ne'er-do-wells, urchins of all sorts, etc. Purely biographically, Evola is fascinating and[ his recent resurgence and resonance with fringe fellas online is worth considering](https://jacobin.com/2022/12/fascism-far-right-evola-bannon-bronze-age-pervert). Just be respectful and kind - it'll be great.

Alright, looking forward to it and reach out to me with any questions in the meantime.

See y'all then!

This week we'll be meeting in Edward’s apartment in Jersey City. A little wine will be provided, but please bring a little extra if you intend to partake so everyone has enough!

As usual, our meetings are structured to build a broader literary community, while also providing a space for sharing work and providing constructive feedback. We balance the social aspect with a focus on encouraging members to produce more, better work, and giving both the pressure and the pleasure of having an audience to test that work out on. While there is typically a majority of narrative prose and poetry, our writers are also essayists, screenwriters, playwrights, or, sometimes, still just figuring it out. As long as you have something you're really working on, we want you to share it.

**Itinerary**
We will be meeting at 292 Barrow Street, Unit 4, Jersey City. When you arrive, just ring the bell and come right up! People are welcome starting at **6 o'clock**, and you can come and write, eat, drink, and socialize until 7 when we will start readings.

At **7 o'clock** we formally get together as a group to listen to readings from those looking for feedback.

* We do not select readers based on order of arrival or a sign-up sheet, but your chances of reading if you show up after 7 may be more slight, so come earlier if you can.
* Each reader gets five (5) minutes to read, so please select a section of reading which is appropriate for that time limit.
* We welcome narrative prose (fiction and non-fiction), poetry, scripts, and essay work, so long as it is writing that you're serious about. The only rule is *don't be boring!*
* We'll then spend another five (5) minutes providing feedback on your work and discussing the craft in general. This is just as important as the reading, and is done as an open conversation. No hand-raising required!
* We try to get to as many people who want to read as we can, so if there are a lot of volunteers we will be very strict on time.

At **9 o'clock** we finish readings and start our formal social hour. Meet new friends, connect with old ones, exchange longer works for review, or just let loose.

The Latte Tours Come to Brooklyn!

What separates a great latte from a good or a bad one? That’s the question at the heart of this new Coffee Hunters event with guest co-host (and frequent Coffee Hunters attendee) Neil Andrews. Neil is a good person to address that question – he’s visited over 230 coffee shops in NYC, putting their lattes to the test and posting reviews on [his website.](https://www.neilandrews.net/nyc/coffee) Having co-hosted latte tours for Coffee Hunters starting in January, he’s excited
to be back for more sequels.

Of all the places he’s visited, only about 40 of them (a mere 20%) have achieved Destination Coffee status – Neil’s designation for places with lattes so good that he would actually travel across the city for them. We’ll be visiting three of those esteemed shops, all in the Bushwick area: Sey, Dayglow and Loveless.

By the end of this tour, you’ll have a sense of the many variables that affect the making of a latte, where things tend to go off the rails, and what absolutely has to happen for the latte to emerge with coveted Destination Coffee status. What better way to spend a morning in April? The cost of the tour will go entirely to coffee and barista tips. There are no refunds if you can't make it, but please cancel your RSVP so someone else can get in!

Note: This same event will be hosted two times (April 20 and April 27). Please only sign up for one.

**We invite you to join us for our latest film history livestream program: "Dolley Madison: America's First Lady", starring Eve Best in the title role.**

The first portion of our two-part program (approximately 15-20 minutes) will be a brief overview of the "Dolley Madison: America's First Lady" film, including the historical context, things to look for, accuracy, etc.
The second portion of our two-part program will be a full screening of the "Dolley Madison: America's First Lady" film (90 minutes).
During and after the screening you'll have the opportunity to discuss the film with your fellow participants via Zoom.

**Dolley Madison** lived through the two wars that established the U.S., was friends with the first 12 Presidents, and watched America evolve from a struggling young republic to the first modern democracy in the world. She was nicknamed “Queen Dolley,” and when she died in 1849 at the age of 81 — one of the last remaining members of the founding generation - Washington City honored her with the largest state funeral the capital had ever seen for a woman.

Born prior to the signing of the Declaration of Independence, Dolley Payne grew up during a time when the country was striving to develop an identity. The daughter of strict Quaker parents, Dolley showed an early interest in contemporary dress and gossip - what her friends considered the evil temptations of the material world. Growing up in the capital city of Philadelphia presented many social opportunities for Dolley, but she acquiesced to her father's wishes that she marry a young Quaker lawyer, John Todd. After only three years of marriage, though, Dolley’s husband died of Yellow Fever in an epidemic that also claimed her youngest son. Widowed and a single parent, she soon met U.S. Congressional Representative James Madison. Four months later, the couple married.

When James Madison became the fourth President of the United States in 1809, Dolley assumed the then ill-defined role of presidential wife. Throughout the world, other nations were ruled by kings and emperors who communicated their power and legitimacy through bejeweled crowns and thrones. In the still new America, and in its capital of Washington, the rules of presidential behavior in a democratic republic had not yet been established by the time the Madisons came to Washington.

As the president's wife, Dolley Madison created a uniquely American style - one that combined power with republican values. She presided over the first Inaugural Ball in Washington, opening it to the public; she took charge of transforming the President's House into a public space that was both elegant and democratic; and as her successors have done ever since, she adopted a social cause of her own, raising funds for an orphanage and advocating for children left parentless by the War of 1812.

Hosting weekly socials where Washington’s elite could mingle in an unofficial capacity, Dolley Madison ushered in a new era of bipartisanship and behind-the-scenes politicking. After the War of 1812, when several politicians talked of abandoning the ravaged capitol and returning to Philadelphia, Dolley Madison continued to host social events, sending a clear message to influential members of Congress and Washington society that Washington was not beyond repair.

Over time, Dolley Madison earned a reputation as skillful diplomat, humanitarian, style icon, and politically savvy hostess. She defined the role of the President's wife and became, in effect, America's first First Lady, and in the process changed the face of the American presidency.

Dolley Madison features Tony Award-nominee Eve Best (Nurse Jackie) as Dolley Madison and Tony Award-winner Jefferson Mays as James Madison (I Am My Own Wife).

The Shroud of Turin is a centuries-old linen cloth that bears the image of a man who appears to have suffered crucifixion, closely resembling biblical descriptions of Jesus Christ’s death. Many believe it to be his actual burial shroud, pointing to its detailed anatomical accuracy and the mysterious way the image was formed. Some researchers suggest that the image could have been created by a burst of energy, possibly linked to the resurrection.

Scientific analysis has attempted to determine its origins, with radiocarbon dating in 1988 suggesting a medieval date, though some argue that contamination or fire damage may have affected the results. Other studies have examined pollen traces, textile patterns, and image formation theories, keeping the debate alive. Regardless of the scientific findings, the Shroud continues to be a profound symbol of faith and an object of fascination, and remains one of the most studied and discussed religious relics in history.

* What characteristics of the Shroud of Turin make it compelling as potential evidence for Jesus’s existence?

* When evaluating the Shroud’s authenticity, how should scientific findings, such as radiocarbon dating, be weighed against historical, religious, and anecdotal evidence?

* If the Shroud were definitively proven to be from the time of Jesus, would that change your perspective on its significance?

* Even if the Shroud is not the actual burial cloth of Jesus, can it still hold symbolic value?

# Introduction to Psychedelic Yoga

Psychedelic Yoga represents a deep integration of traditional yogic methods with intentional psychedelic practice. Far beyond simply combining substances with stretching, this approach draws from yoga's complete system—spanning breathwork, meditation, movement, visualization, and embodied awareness—to support three interconnected goals: ***healing, spiritual growth, and creative flow.***

For healing work, Psychedelic Yoga provides tools to access and process emotions stored in the body's energy centers. By bringing awareness to the chakras and using specialized breathing techniques, we can release blockages that maintain suffering. Whether working with psychedelics or practicing these methods on their own, these approaches help balance the body-mind system at its foundation.

Spiritual exploration becomes more accessible when we understand consciousness through direct experience rather than abstract concepts. Dream Yoga practices, visualization techniques, and meditation methods from various traditions create bridges between ordinary and non-ordinary states. These practices help us recognize how mental patterns create separation and suffering, opening doorways to profound insights about our true nature.

Creative flow emerges naturally when we restore "Child's Mind" and release the energetic patterns that maintain limiting mental habits. Through specific asanas, mudras, and breath practices, we can cultivate states of heightened awareness where innovation flourishes. The symbiotic relationship between psychedelic experiences and yogic practice creates optimal conditions for learning and creative breakthroughs.

Throughout this workshop, we'll explore practical techniques from these three domains, experiencing how they support each other and form a comprehensive approach to consciousness exploration. *Whether you're interested in enhancing psychedelic journeys or accessing similar states through breath and awareness alone, these methods offer valuable tools for your path!*

Each of the composers on this program went through an Expressionist phase after they abandoned Late Romanticism and before they embraced twelve-tone music. During this period, they explored how music can be used to communicate emotional disequilibrium, dreams, and subconscious experience when it becomes untethered from conventional tonality. While Expressionism shared with Impressionism some of the same motivations and the preoccupation with tone color, Schoenberg, Berg, and Webern followed a different path from Debussy's.

Join our host Robert to examine some of the preeminent works in this genre, including *Pierrot Lunaire* and *Wozzeck*. Our focus will be how to listen to this kind of music and to examine how it manages to express anything without a tonal framework.

What is 'self-love'? Many people struggle with understanding self-love, mistaking it for selfishness, arrogance, or indulgence, which can lead to cycles of guilt, burnout, or unfulfilled relationships. Solutions such as positive affirmations, self-care routines, and boundary-setting have been offered, but they often feel superficial or fail to address deeper emotional wounds. How can we cultivate genuine self-love that strengthens our well-being and relationships without falling into the traps of narcissism, avoidance, or entitlement? Join us as we break down the myths, explore the challenges, and uncover what true self-love really looks like.

* How do you personally define self-love, and how does your definition compare to how society portrays it?
* Where do you think the boundaries of self-love lie? At what point does it shift into something else, like entitlement or even narcissism?

Surprisingly, many users still rely on outdated keyword-based systems. Why do these “old” tools remain effective? Because humans compensate for their limitations. Users refine their queries, test synonyms, or chain searches together. This reveals a critical insight: the biggest gains in search won’t come from marginally improving retrieval models, but from employing search agents.

Join us for an exciting session on Agentic Search, where we will explore how search engines can go beyond simple query matching to strategically solve complex problems. We will dive into the limitations of traditional keyword-based search systems and introduce the concept of search agents. Learn how these agents can decompose complex queries, iterate through hypotheses, and synthesize insights across multiple sources to provide more relevant answers.

What You’ll Learn:

* Understand the evolution of search from keyword-based systems to semantic search.
* Discover why traditional search models are reaching their limits and how agentic search can break through them.
* Learn how search agents can decompose queries into sub-questions and synthesize insights from multiple sources.
* Explore real-world examples of agentic search in action.
* Understand how this paradigm can redefine the future of search, delivering results that are not only more accurate but also more insightful.

* Uncover common failure modes like infinite loops, brittle planning, and tool misuse — and how to spot them early.
* Preview the need for better evaluation methods in agentic systems and why tracing and observability are crucial.
* Watch a live walkthrough of a simple agent trace using Arize Phoenix to understand what is an AI agent and how evaluation and debugging works in practice.

* **Defining the VMO charter and governance model** using AI-generated frameworks.
* **Identifying and prioritizing value streams** with AI-driven clustering and backlog analysis.
* **Automating funding forecasts and scenario planning** based on historical data.
* **Enhancing decision-making with AI-powered risk assessments** and real-time portfolio insights.
* **Leveraging AI for reporting, alignment and continuous improvement.**

Our discussion's focus isn’t about theory—it’s about execution. By the end, you’ll have a **concrete AI-assisted approach** to setting up and scaling an Agile VMO that improves agility, governance, and value delivery.

**About our Speaker:**
John is LitheSpeed’s VP, Consulting, as well as an Enterprise Agile Consultant, Coach and Trainer. He leverages more than two decades of executive leadership experience as a CIO, CTO and Vice President of Technology, helping enterprises deliver business value through agile and lean approaches.
